resources.string: Log your period to get started
Tap Period started on the first day of your period. You can also add earlier periods on the calendar.
An estimate only. It can\'t be used to prevent pregnancy.
Based on your typical cycle. Predictions get more personal as you log periods.
Still on your period? Log today
How are you feeling? Log symptoms, mood, energy and more.
Hormone levels are at their lowest and energy may dip. Rest, warmth and gentle movement can help with cramps.
Estrogen rises as your body prepares to release an egg. Many people notice their energy and mood lifting.
Around your estimated ovulation. Some people notice clearer, stretchier discharge or a twinge on one side. This is an estimate and can\'t be used to prevent pregnancy.
Progesterone rises after ovulation. In the days before your period you might notice bloating, tender breasts or mood changes.
Most hormonal birth control prevents ovulation, so Cadence doesn\'t show cycle phases or ovulation estimates. You can still log bleeding and see when to expect it.
Your period was expected around now. Cycles naturally vary by a few days from one month to the next.
Cycles vary for many reasons, including stress, illness, travel and changes in weight or exercise. If you might be pregnant, a test can tell you for sure.
Each time you log a period, Cadence learns your rhythm. After two cycles, predictions are based on your own history.
No break on continuous use, so Cadence doesn\'t predict bleeding. Log any bleeding as usual.
A withdrawal bleed usually comes during the break. It can be light, or not come at all.
Next break %1$s to %2$s, when a bleed is likely
If you missed one, check your pack\'s leaflet or ask a pharmacist what to do. You may need extra protection.
Using a pill, patch or ring?
Add it in Settings to check off doses, get reminders, and see when your break-week bleed is likely.

A period usually lasts 2 to 7 days, and most people lose only a few tablespoons of blood. Bleeding for more than 7 days, or needing a new pad or tampon every hour or two, is worth mentioning to a doctor.

This phase starts on the first day of your period, as follicles in the ovaries begin to mature. It\'s the part of the cycle whose length varies most, which is why cycles differ from person to person and month to month.

An egg lives for about a day after it\'s released, but sperm can survive for several days, so the most fertile days are the ones just before ovulation. Ovulation can move from cycle to cycle, which is why Cadence\'s date is only an estimate.
This phase is the most consistent, usually around 12 to 14 days. Premenstrual symptoms typically ease once your period starts. If they affect your daily life, a doctor can help.

Combined pills, patches and rings work mainly by stopping ovulation. The bleed during a break is a withdrawal bleed, caused by the drop in hormones, rather than a true period. Many people can safely skip breaks, but check with your clinician or pharmacist before changing how you take yours.
Source: NHS, \"Periods and fertility in the menstrual cycle\".
